---
title: "Prediction intervals with quantile models"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

Quantile regression gives a direct path to prediction intervals inside DuckDB: train several pinball models, check coverage, and optionally apply split-conformal calibration. Export with `keep_columns` so scored rows keep their identity keys.

```sql
LOAD duckboost;

CREATE TABLE series AS
SELECT
	i::DOUBLE AS x,
	(0.5 * i + 3.0 * sin(i / 5.0) + (i % 7) * 0.2)::DOUBLE AS y,
	i AS id
FROM range(1, 101) t(i);

CREATE TABLE quantile_models AS
SELECT
	duckboost_train(y, [x], MAP {
		'objective': 'quantile', 'quantile_alpha': '0.05',
		'n_estimators': '30', 'max_depth': '3', 'feature_names': 'x'
	}) AS q05,
	duckboost_train(y, [x], MAP {
		'objective': 'quantile', 'quantile_alpha': '0.50',
		'n_estimators': '30', 'max_depth': '3', 'feature_names': 'x'
	}) AS q50,
	duckboost_train(y, [x], MAP {
		'objective': 'quantile', 'quantile_alpha': '0.95',
		'n_estimators': '30', 'max_depth': '3', 'feature_names': 'x'
	}) AS q95
FROM series;
```

Empirical coverage and mean interval width on the training rows:

```sql
SELECT
	round(avg((y >= lo AND y <= hi)::INTEGER), 2) AS coverage,
	round(avg(hi - lo), 2) AS mean_width,
	round(avg((lo <= mid AND mid <= hi)::INTEGER), 2) AS ordered_bands
FROM (
	SELECT
		s.y,
		duckboost_predict(m.q05, [s.x]) AS lo,
		duckboost_predict(m.q50, [s.x]) AS mid,
		duckboost_predict(m.q95, [s.x]) AS hi
	FROM series s, quantile_models m
);
```

Pinball loss via `duckboost_evaluate` follows the stored `objective_alpha` when `metric` is `auto`:

```sql
SELECT
	duckboost_evaluate_agg(model, y, [x]) AS auto_pinball,
	duckboost_evaluate_agg(model, y, [x], MAP {'metric': 'pinball'}) AS pinball
FROM q90, series;
```

When independently trained quantiles cross, enforce order with `least` / `greatest` before reporting the interval:

```sql
SELECT
	id,
	least(lo, hi) AS lower,
	greatest(lo, hi) AS upper
FROM (
	SELECT
		s.id,
		duckboost_predict(m.q05, [s.x]) AS lo,
		duckboost_predict(m.q95, [s.x]) AS hi
	FROM series s, quantile_models m
);
```

## Split-conformal calibration

Hold out a calibration fold, compute absolute residual scores against the quantile band, and take the conformal quantile of those scores. Adding that width to every prediction interval restores finite-sample coverage under exchangeability, at the cost of wider intervals.

```sql
-- Example shape (fill in with your calibration split):
-- score_i = greatest(q_lo(x_i) - y_i, y_i - q_hi(x_i))
-- q_hat = quantile_cont(score, 1 - alpha) on the calibration fold
-- interval = [q_lo - q_hat, q_hi + q_hat]
```

## Deploy with identity columns

For scoring jobs, keep the row id beside the prediction so results join back without relying on row order:

```sql
SELECT duckboost_to_sql(
	model,
	'series',
	['x'],
	MAP {
		'separate_trees': 'false',
		'prediction_alias': 'q50',
		'keep_columns': 'id'
	}
) AS export_sql
FROM q50;
```

## Scale note

The native trainer buffers every training row and its bin ids in memory, then finds splits from histograms (including oblivious / symmetric growth). Training is single-threaded. `duckboost_predict` caches a parsed model within each execution chunk when the JSON repeats; for large scoring jobs prefer `duckboost_to_sql` (optionally with `keep_columns` / `proba`) and run the generated SQL without the extension.
